result.title: Generative Active Learning for Label-Efficient Pan-Organ Ultrasound Diagnosis
result.summary: Medical ultrasound (US) enables real-time, non-invasive diagnosis, yet building US-based AI systems is limited by data scarcity, costly expert annotation, and limited cross-center generalizability. Privacy constraints and instance-level reporting hinder the collection of diverse abnormal cases and frame-level labels, while repeated retraining for new centers increases computational cost. We introduce EvoDiff, a generative active learning framework that integrates diffusion modelling with information-theoretic objectives, evolutionary search, and curriculum-based sampling to select informative samples across heterogeneous US datasets. EvoDiff formulates sample selection as a generate-to-retrieve process, in which diffusion-based optimization in feature space guided by information gain produces synthetic probes, and only the real unlabeled samples retrieved by these probes are annotated and used for downstream training. Across six benchmarks covering fifteen datasets and 16,696 images, we evaluate EvoDiff on convolutional network and transformer-based foundation model. EvoDiff approaches fully supervised performance with substantially fewer labels, outperforms active learning baselines, and improves foundation model generalization under cross-domain external validation on unseen cohorts. A reader study with six radiologists indicates the potential to support clinical annotation workflows, with a model-based estimated 24% to 84% reduction in annotation workload at matched downstream performance.

AI.brief_summary: EvoDiff 提出生成式主动学习框架，将扩散模型、信息论目标、进化搜索与课程采样结合，在特征空间生成合成探针以检索真实未标注超声图像进行标注，并在多数据集上评估标签效率与跨中心泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其信息增益驱动的「生成探针—检索样本」获取方式，可能与 LVR 中主动筛选视觉证据、按信息价值决定采集的策略形成概念类比，可供核查；但该方法作用于训练数据标注层面，而非推理期 latent 状态。
